Subject: Spike in inference 503s and 99th latency this morning

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a surge of 503s and ~30–40% tail latency increase across our inference calls to redwood-us-1 around 09:45 PDT. Error rates peaked for ~18 minutes but customers are noticing intermittent timeouts since then. Attached a small bundle with sample request IDs, client-side traces, and some truncated server responses (error-snippets.zip).

What we see: 
- Elevated 503s correlated with a handful of backend IPs (10.4.x.x) returning TCP RSTs.
- Traceroutes show an asymmetric path through a cloud-edge proxy that looks different from Tuesday.
- No config changes on our side, but we did get a NAT rotation notice from our infra provider around 08:55.

Can you confirm whether Redwood changed any peering or proxy rules in us-west-2 this morning? We need an ETA; this is customer-impacting and finance will ask about credits if outages persist.

Thanks,

Marissa / Alex — quick triage notes from the infra side (i copied relevant logs inline):

Summary: we observed a series of short-lived egress queueing events on the us-west-2 peering frontends that correlate with NAT health flaps at the third-party edge. During those windows, proxy workers dropped inflight responses leading to 503s and TCP resets visible in your captures.

What I pulled: 
- Proxy backlog metric (redwood-proxy-usw2): spike from 12->120 inflight requests at 09:44–09:52 PT.
- Upstream peering routes: a small subset of packets took an alternate path through a partner edge (cloudops-02) which had an MTU mismatch and retried.
- We saw an ingress->egress path asymmetry: traceroutes from our frontend to your client IPs show a different last-hop set than monday baseline.

Immediate asks for Alex: 
- Please confirm whether your firewall rules dropped ICMP or changed MSS settings after the reported NAT rotation. That can cause the MTU retrains.
- If you can, upload the tcpdump you mentioned (client-side).

Actions we’re taking: 
- Flushing and pinning peering route to fallback edge for Midsignal traffic in us-west-2 to avoid cloudops-02 for now.
- Increasing proxy worker headroom and enabling a temporary connection retry reduction (hoping to reduce 503s).
- Collecting pcap and flow log slices (I’m attaching our flow-logs snippet to the shared Drive).

I’ll keep this thread updated with whether the pinned route holds; early telemetry shows error-rate dropping but not zero.

—Sean Gallagher
Principle SRE, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Marissa / Sean / Alex — this is CloudOps Edge support. We rotated a NAT cluster in us-west-2 at 08:55 due to degraded health on one node; the rotation briefly moved some customer flows through cloudops-02 which was under higher CPU and experienced packet fragmentation for some jumbo frames. We’ve replicated the issue in staging and captured flow logs.

Key findings: 
- The NAT rotation coincided with an MTU negotiation fallback on ~2% of flows; these exhibited retransmits and occasional TCP RSTs.
- Our edge team applied an immediate MTU clamp and rebalanced sessions, which reduced the fragmentation events.

Artifacts: attached flow-logs-20270924.json and a packet sample we captured. We will keep cloudops-02 in reduced load until you confirm stability.

Ticket: INF-4452 opened (link in email chain).

Regards,
